subject: saving a plot as "ggp" for future use

messages.author: 72edac7635982d8b
messages.subject: saving a plot as "ggp" for future use
parts:
Hi,
Does anyone knows how can I save/load a complete plot structure for
future use/editing with a single command line ? I can do similar job,
but only inside the Deducer GUI, using save/load with "*.ggp"
attributes. In the other hand, "ggsave" only stores the plot image,
not its structure.Thanks a lot,
Jose Mauricio

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: saving a plot as "ggp" for future use
parts:
Hi Jose,
I don't know what ggp is, but you can save ggplot objects just like
any other thing in R. See ?save

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 72edac7635982d8b
messages.subject: Re: saving a plot as "ggp" for future use
parts:
Thanks Professor Wickham and folks,
I perceive that the "ggp" object belongs to the inner structure of the
Deducer package, not the ggplot2 itself, where it can be retrieve for
editing/use as a file outside a particular workspace. A similar work
can be done with an R script, and even by the use of expression/eval
functions, but in the latter case with local/ global variables as
targets. In this sense I think, maybe, that an R script takes more
advantages for construction of (very) complex grobs as templates with
different datasets. Thanks again to all and have a nice week,
Jose Mauricio

Prof. Dr. José Maurício Schneedorf FS
Bioelectrochemistry Lab
Federal University of Alfenas
Minas Gerais, Brazil
